x: Natalie Law has moved up an age group since last season and now finds herself facing Seniors in SL competition but with new member Sabrina Scott for company, the sprints became a happy hunting ground in the quest for points.

U20W ~ Sabrina Scott For the following awards, fulfilling the basic criteria does not guarantee an award - the number of competitors taking part and regular support of the Club are also taken into consideration and all must have achieved AAA Grade I performances.
Sprinter Sabrina Scott turned out while in the 3,000 metres we were treated to a dominating run from Samantha Northey as she ran away from the combined Division One and Six fields to win by a street.

Sabrina Scott was awesome in the 200 metres setting a new personal best. When the results came in from around the South we found that only Enfield and Huntingdon had kept their unbeaten records while we had slipped to 8th overall – still within range of a top five position and promotion.

Sabrina Scott's sprinting and jumping contributed tremendously to the score (as it did in each of the following matches) and the 3,000 metres turned out to be really exciting as Sam Northey attempted to blast away from the field with two laps to go, only to get caught by the experienced Highgate run…

The jumps, too, gave us some good scores with Julia Cockram taking the senior high jump and pole vault, Jacqui Smiter taking the 'B' high jump and Sabrina Scott notching up yet another long jump victory.
Sabrina Scott gained good points in the sprints and then took just two jumps to mop up the 'B' long jump while Angela Abrams gained maximum points in the 'A' competition.
It was touch and go throughout the afternoon with good points collected by Sabrina Scott in the sprints and Sarah Roberts in the 400 metres and triple jump.
